lessons.title: Climate Change and its Effects on the Environment

pages.title: What you will learn
pages.body:
🎯 **By the end of this lesson you will be able to:**
- Describe the signs of climate change.
- Search for causes and effects of climate change and present a report.
- Explain how countries in the continents are adapting to climate change, for example tree planting and legislation on bush burning.

pages.title: What is Climate Change?
pages.body: Climate change refers to significant, long term shifts in temperature, rainfall patterns and weather conditions across the world, largely driven by increased greenhouse gases in the atmosphere. While weather describes short term daily conditions, climate describes the average weather patterns of a region over many years, and climate change describes how these long term patterns are shifting, mainly due to human activities that release extra greenhouse gases such as carbon (IV) oxide and methane.

pages.title: Signs of Climate Change
pages.body: Rising temperatures, melting ice, changing rainfall patterns, and rising sea levels are four widely observed signs that scientists use as evidence that the climate is changing, as shown below.

pages.title: Causes and Effects of Climate Change
pages.body:
Burning fossil fuels, deforestation, industrial and agricultural practices, and improper waste disposal are four major human activities linked to climate change, each contributing additional greenhouse gases to the atmosphere, as summarised in the table below.

| **CAUSE OF CLIMATE CHANGE** | **EFFECT ON THE ENVIRONMENT** |
|---|---|
| **Burning fossil fuels for energy and transport** | Increases greenhouse gases, trapping more heat and raising average temperatures |
| **Deforestation and bush burning** | Reduces the number of trees available to absorb carbon (IV) oxide, worsening warming |
| **Industrial and agricultural practices** | Release additional greenhouse gases, such as methane, contributing to warming |
| **Improper waste disposal** | Decomposing waste in landfills can release methane, a powerful greenhouse gas |

The combined effect of these activities is a gradual warming of the earth's atmosphere, which in turn disrupts weather patterns, affects agriculture, threatens coastal communities, and increases the frequency of extreme weather events such as severe storms and prolonged droughts.

lessons.title: How Countries are Adapting to Climate Change

pages.title: How Countries are Adapting to Climate Change
pages.body: Tree planting, legislation on bush burning, improved farming practices, and renewable energy investment are examples of adaptation measures being adopted by countries across different continents in response to climate change. Many African countries, including Ghana, have introduced tree planting initiatives to help restore forest cover and absorb more carbon (IV) oxide from the atmosphere. Legislation restricting bush burning aims to reduce both the direct release of greenhouse gases and the loss of trees that would otherwise help absorb them. Similar adaptation efforts can be seen in other tropical countries facing comparable climate related challenges, showing that climate change is a shared, global concern requiring coordinated action.

pages.title: Look at the picture
pages.body:
[[img:i8b0306840|Fig 7.1  Common signs of climate change observed around the world]]

Notice that these signs are connected. Rising temperatures contribute to melting ice, which contributes to rising sea levels, while changing rainfall patterns can bring both more frequent droughts and more intense flooding to different regions at different times.

pages.title: Going further
pages.body:
> 💡 **Going further**

International agreements, such as the Paris Agreement, bring countries together to commit to reducing greenhouse gas emissions and supporting each other in adapting to climate change. Ghana has taken part in such international efforts alongside its own domestic programmes, showing that addressing climate change effectively requires action at the individual, national and international levels all working together.

lessons.title: Climate Change Adaptation and Green Economy Actions

pages.title: What you will learn
pages.body:
🎯 **By the end of this lesson you will be able to:**
- Describe climate change adaptation measures that can be applied in the community.
- Discuss mitigation strategies that your community can adopt to reduce the effects of climate change.

pages.title: Adaptation Versus Mitigation
pages.body: Adaptation and mitigation are two related but distinct approaches used to respond to climate change. Adaptation involves adjusting how communities live and work so they can cope better with the effects of climate change that are already happening or expected, such as changing farming practices to suit less predictable rainfall. Mitigation involves taking action to reduce the causes of climate change itself, mainly by reducing the amount of greenhouse gases released into the atmosphere, such as by planting trees or switching to renewable energy.

questions.q: Adaptation to climate change mainly involves
o: Adjusting how communities live and work to cope with its effects
Ignoring the effects of climate change completely
Reducing the causes of climate change only
questions.e: Adaptation involves adjusting how communities live and work so they can cope better with the effects of climate change that are already happening or expected, such as changing farming practices to suit less predictable rainfall.

questions.q: Mitigation of climate change mainly involves
o: Adjusting only to its effects with no other action
Reducing the causes of climate change, such as greenhouse gas emissions
questions.e: Mitigation involves taking action to reduce the causes of climate change itself, mainly by reducing the amount of greenhouse gases released into the atmosphere, such as by planting trees or switching to renewable energy.

pages.title: Climate Change Adaptation Measures
pages.body:
Drought resistant crops, improved water management, early warning systems, resilient building design, and income diversification are five adaptation measures that can help a community cope better with the effects of climate change, as summarised in the table below.

| **ADAPTATION MEASURE** | **HOW IT HELPS THE COMMUNITY COPE WITH CLIMATE CHANGE** |
|---|---|
| **Drought resistant crop varieties** | Allow farmers to maintain yields even during periods of reduced or unpredictable rainfall |
| **Improved water storage and irrigation** | Helps communities manage water supply during both droughts and heavy rainfall |
| **Early warning systems for extreme weather** | Gives communities time to prepare for floods, storms or heatwaves |
| **Building on higher ground or with flood resistant designs** | Reduces damage to homes and property from flooding linked to changing rainfall patterns |
| **Diversifying income sources** | Reduces a family's dependence on a single crop or activity that could be affected by climate related shocks |

pages.title: Mitigation Strategies for Communities
pages.body:
Planting trees, reducing bush burning, adopting renewable energy, managing waste properly, and improving energy efficiency are five mitigation strategies that communities can realistically adopt to help reduce the overall effects of climate change, as summarised in the table below.

| **MITIGATION STRATEGY** | **HOW IT REDUCES THE EFFECTS OF CLIMATE CHANGE** |
|---|---|
| **Planting and protecting trees** | Absorbs carbon (IV) oxide from the atmosphere and restores natural habitats |
| **Reducing bush burning** | Prevents unnecessary release of greenhouse gases and loss of vegetation |
| **Switching to renewable energy sources** | Reduces reliance on burning fossil fuels, which release greenhouse gases |
| **Proper waste management** | Reduces methane released from decomposing waste in poorly managed landfills |
| **Energy efficient practices** | Reduces the amount of fuel or electricity needed, lowering associated emissions |

pages.title: The Green Economy
pages.body: A green economy is an economic system that aims to improve human wellbeing and reduce poverty while significantly lowering environmental risks and reducing harm to natural resources. Green economy actions often combine both adaptation and mitigation, for example by supporting renewable energy businesses that create jobs while reducing emissions, or by promoting sustainable agriculture that maintains food production while protecting soil and forests.

pages.title: Look at the picture
pages.body:
[[img:i8b0306840|Fig 7.1  Signs of climate change that adaptation and mitigation measures aim to address]]

Notice that adaptation measures respond directly to these signs, such as building flood resistant homes in response to changing rainfall, while mitigation measures aim to slow or reduce the underlying causes driving these signs in the first place.

pages.title: Going further
pages.body:
> 💡 **Going further**

Ghana has developed national policies aimed at supporting green economic growth, including initiatives to promote renewable energy, sustainable agriculture, and reforestation. These policies recognise that responding effectively to climate change is not only an environmental necessity but can also create new economic opportunities, particularly for young people entering fields such as renewable energy installation, sustainable farming, and environmental management.
